Yes—almost certainly.

At **15.2° altitude** in the **east (azimuth 87.2°)**, the Moon is comfortably above the astronomical horizon, though still fairly low. At **98% illumination**, it is essentially full and extremely bright. With the Sun **30.8° below the horizon**, the sky is fully dark, and clear conditions make visibility excellent.

Assuming no nearby obstruction—such as buildings, trees, or terrain blocking the eastern sky—you should see it easily with unaided vision. Look **almost due east**, about **15° above the horizon** (roughly one and a half fist-widths at arm’s length). Atmospheric haze might dim or redden it somewhat, but would be unlikely to prevent detection.
